subject: Everledger capacity certification: benchmarking & acceptance
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Santos <miguel@everledger.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Everledger capacity certification: benchmarking & acceptance

Hi Miguel —

Following our onboarding call, attaching the proposed capacity certification plan and sample traffic templates so we can align on test shape, targets, and evidence for sign-off. Key asks from our side:

- Confirm the peak QPS you expect for the initial 24/7 production window and any planned burst windows (we put a placeholder of 120 QPS).
- Confirm acceptable latency SLOs (we suggest P95 <= 200ms, P99 <= 450ms for the first rollout).
- Share a preferred test week (we suggested June 30–July 2).

Attachments: everledger-capacity-certification-plan.pdf, sample-traffic-templates.csv

Quick summary of the plan:
- Day 1: Synthetic baseline run (steady-state at target QPS, 90-minute window).
- Day 2: Stress runs with spike windows and KV/prefix cache disabled to validate cold-path behavior.
- Day 3: Replay of a representative production traffic CSV (you provide) plus verification that failover to lower-tier model maintains functional correctness.

Monica — please confirm test runner, exact endpoints to hit, and how we’ll deliver the artifacts (we usually deliver a zipped results bundle + Grafana snapshots).

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
From: Miguel Santos <miguel@everledger.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Anya Volkova <anya@everledger.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Everledger capacity certification: benchmarking & acceptance

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the plan, this looks good. A few clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

1) Peak QPS: our immediate target is 85 QPS, but we want to validate headroom up to 200 QPS for burst scenarios.
2) User-facing SLO: we'd prefer P95 <= 250ms, P99 <= 500ms for the first 2 weeks in prod; if Redwood can consistently hit 200ms P95 we may tighten later.
3) Data: we can provide a traffic sample (anonymized) — I'll send that by Friday.

We can target June 30–July 2; please confirm your windows in PST. Also, can you confirm whether the stress run will include simultaneous embedding requests (we use both generation and embeddings in parallel)?

Regards,
Miguel
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Everledger

---
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Santos <miguel@everledger.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Everledger capacity certification: benchmarking & acceptance

Great — thanks Miguel. To confirm:

- Test targets we'll run: steady-state 85 QPS, validated headroom up to 200 QPS.
- Latency acceptance: baseline goal P95 <= 200ms (we'll report both your requested thresholds and our baseline).
- Stress will include mixed-traffic (generation + embeddings) with a 20% embeddings ratio; Monica will share the exact runner flags to ensure we hit the right mix.

Monica — can you provision the runner for PST windows:
- Jun 30 14:00–16:00 PST: Baseline 90min run (we'll shorten to fit calendar)
- Jul 1 09:00–12:00 PST: Spike/stress permutations
- Jul 2 11:00–13:00 PST: Replay of traffic CSV + failover scenarios

Laura — I'll need you to own acceptance criteria signoff process and capture the evidence checklist (Grafana snapshots, latency histograms, token-cost breakdown, and the zipped results file).

Ben

---
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Santos <miguel@everledger.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Everledger capacity certification: benchmarking & acceptance

Hi all —

Runner details and test artifacts below. I attached the test script and a small helper CSV template. We will run from our dedicated test harness in us-west-2 and stream metrics to a temporary Grafana dashboard for you to watch live.

Runner commands (example):
- ./redwood-test-script.sh --endpoint https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate --qps 85 --duration 5400 --embed-ratio 0.2 --payload-template sample-traffic-templates.csv
- Spike profile (for 2-minute bursts): --spike --spike-peaks 200,180,150 --spike-duration 120

Evidence we will collect:
- Raw logs and token-level traces
- Prometheus/Grafana metric snapshots (P50/P95/P99 latency, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization)
- Combined cost breakdown per 1M tokens for each run (to validate unit economics)

Attachments: redwood-test-script.sh, sample-traffic-templates.csv

I'll spin up the runner on Jun 30 at 14:00 PST and invite you to the Grafana view (you'll get a link shortly). If you prefer a different timezone anchor, say so and we can shift.

Thanks,
Monica
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
From: Miguel Santos <miguel@everledger.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Everledger capacity certification: benchmarking & acceptance (results)

Team —

Thanks for running the tests. We reviewed the artifacts this afternoon. High-level results:

- Baseline (85 QPS steady): P95 = 185ms, P99 = 420ms, error rate 0.02% — PASSED against our interim threshold (P95<=250ms).
- Burst/headroom: sustained at 200 QPS for 2-minute spikes; P95 rose to 260ms and P99 to 530ms during the heaviest peaks. We consider headroom validated but will request a follow-up optimization for sustained 200 QPS windows.
- Embeddings + generation mixed run: no functional regressions observed; cost-per-1M-tokens reported in attached cost breakdown.

We are comfortable to move to a phased production ramp with the condition that Redwood teams track a perf-optimization ticket to tighten P95 under sustained burst load. Laura, please open the final acceptance form and mark the run artifacts as attached — we'll sign once the follow-up item is in the backlog.

Attachments received: test-results-20260701.zip (logs + Grafana snapshots + cost breakdown)

Regards,
Miguel
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Everledger

---
